IN.name: India

laws.name: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
laws.citation: Act No. 22 of 2023; consent (s.6), children (s.9), transfers (s.16) operative ~13 May 2027

laws.name: IT (Reasonable Security Practices and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011
laws.citation: G.S.R. 313(E), 11 Apr 2011, under IT Act s.43A; r.3 health = SPDI, r.5 consent, r.7 transfer

laws.name: Telemedicine Practice Guidelines, 2020
laws.citation: Appendix 5, IMC (Professional Conduct) Regulations 2002; para 5.4 bars AI from counselling or prescribing

laws.name: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
laws.citation: G.S.R. 846(E), 13 Nov 2025; Rules 3, 5-16 from 13 May 2027

healthcare_rules: Refer to a registered medical practitioner (RMP) for anything about the person's own condition; AI platforms may not counsel patients in India (Telemedicine Practice Guidelines 2020, para 5.4).
Use Indian medicine names, and say when a medicine is prescription-only in India (Schedule H, H1 or X); never help someone get one without a prescription.
Refuse any request to learn or choose a baby's sex, and name no method at all - medical, folk or home test - not even to debunk it; India's PCPNDT Act bans communicating sex determination.
Do not present any drug, supplement or AYUSH remedy as a cure, especially for diabetes, cancer, obesity or sexual or fertility problems; India's Drugs and Magic Remedies Act bans such claims.
guidance_rules: Do not call these conversations counselling, therapy or treatment; describe them as wellbeing or mentoring support, since Indian rules bar AI from counselling and reserve psychologist titles to RCI-registered professionals.

When someone describes lasting low mood, anxiety, sleeplessness or other signs a professional should see, suggest Tele-MANAS - the government's free, round-the-clock mental health line in Indian languages - or a professional.
IN.notes: Health data is 'sensitive' only under the SPDI Rules 2011, until DPDP s.44(2) repeals IT Act s.43A (~13 May 2027); DPDP has no sensitive tier, so reclassify to 'personal' then. DPDP notice, consent, children and transfer duties start ~13 May 2027 (some trackers say 14 May). SPDI reach over a US-only company is arguable. Board still unstaffed (Lok Sabha, 12 Aug 2026). SC challenge reported as W.P.(C) 177/2026, no stay (low confidence). DMR Act, NMC Act s.34, CDSCO SaMD and MeitY 2024 advisory were not re-fetched (medium). Grievance contact (SPDI r.5(9), DPDP Rule 9): published in the privacy policy and on the consent card; the Grievance Officer's name must be added there.
IN.complaints_to: the Data Protection Board of India

PK.name: Pakistan

laws.name: Pakistan Medical and Dental Council Act, 2022
laws.citation: Practice of medicine and prescribing reserved to registered practitioners

laws.name: Drugs Act 1976 / DRAP Act 2012 and Medical Devices Rules 2017
laws.citation: Drug advertising restrictions; software for diagnosis, monitoring or treatment may be a device

laws.name: Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 (PECA)
laws.citation: Act XL of 2016, amended 2025; s.16 unauthorised use of identity information

laws.name: Personal Data Protection Bill, 2023 (draft, not enacted)
laws.citation: MoITT draft, Cabinet-approved July 2023; would make health data sensitive

healthcare_rules: Refer anything about the person's own condition to a PMDC-registered doctor, and do not call this a consultation, telemedicine, diagnosis or triage; in Pakistan those labels risk DRAP device and healthcare-commission rules.
Do not promote branded medicines or make cure or efficacy claims about any medicine; DRAP rules restrict drug advertising to the public in Pakistan.
PK.regulator: No data protection authority (proposed National Commission for Personal Data Protection not set up); health: DRAP (https://www.dra.gov.pk) and PMDC (https://www.pmdc.pk)
PK.notes: No data protection statute in force, so health_data is 'personal'. Draft PDP Bill 2023 not enacted per Chambers and DLA Piper (Mar 2026), but Apr-Oct 2026 news was not checked. If enacted, health data becomes 'sensitive' and could be designated 'critical personal data' that must stay in Pakistan, which would change storage. DRAP, PMDC and IHRA sites were unreachable, so the health-sector rules come from background knowledge (low confidence). Attempted-suicide decriminalisation (2022) unverified.

BD.name: Bangladesh

laws.name: Personal Data Protection Act, 2026
laws.citation: Act No. 63 of 2026; ss.2(21)-(22) health data sensitive, s.7 explicit consent, s.9 children, s.29 transfers

laws.name: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 2023
laws.citation: Act No. 29 of 2023; s.2(33) software as medical device, s.40 prescription-only, s.71 advertising

laws.name: Mental Health Act, 2018
laws.citation: Act No. 60 of 2018; s.2(6) treatment includes advice and counselling

laws.name: Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council Act, 2010

healthcare_rules: Say when a medicine is prescription-only in Bangladesh (non-OTC drugs, Drugs and Cosmetics Act 2023 s.40), and never promote a drug or claim it cures or treats a disease (s.71).
guidance_rules: Do not frame replies as advice or counselling for a mental health condition; Bangladesh's Mental Health Act 2018 s.2(6) treats advice and counselling as treatment under psychiatrist supervision.
If someone mentions a suicide attempt, respond supportively and do not raise legality or imply it will be reported; attempted suicide may still be an offence in Bangladesh (Penal Code s.309).
BD.regulator: National Data Management Authority (no verified website); health: DGDA (https://dgda.gov.bd) and BMDC (https://bmdc.org.bd)
BD.notes: PDPA 2026 applies extraterritorially (s.1(2)(c)). US transfer allowed with consent (s.29(3)), but adequacy regulations (s.29(4)) are not issued and the s.29(1) data-classification schedule was not seen; if health data is classed 'restricted', storage needs revisiting. Large-volume sensitive transfers must be notified to the Authority (s.29(6)). The repealed Feb 2026 ordinance's localisation clause was dropped. Fines, complaints and CDO duty start ~May 2027. Texts read via machine translation of the Bangla. Penal Code s.309 repeal not checked.

LK.name: Sri Lanka

laws.name: Personal Data Protection Act, No. 9 of 2022
laws.citation: s.56 special categories incl. health; Schedules II-III consent; Parts I and III in force 1 Jan 2027 (Gazette 2498/16)

laws.name: Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act, No. 22 of 2025
laws.citation: Substituted s.26 (cross-border: explicit consent after risk notice, s.26(3)(a))

laws.name: National Medicines Regulatory Authority Act, No. 5 of 2015
laws.citation: Software medical devices; ss.55, 79 promotion limits

healthcare_rules: Do not recommend or promote a specific medicine or medical device as a treatment, prevention or cure; Sri Lanka's NMRA Act (ss.55, 79) restricts such promotion to the public.
LK.regulator: Data Protection Authority of Sri Lanka (https://www.dpa.gov.lk)
LK.notes: Research gives a child age of 16 (s.56); raised to 18 per product policy. Substantive duties (Parts I and III, incl. s.26 transfers) commence 1 Jan 2027 (Gazette 2498/16, 22 Jul 2026); Part II rights, Part IV and Part VII penalties still await an Order. US transfer route: explicit consent after a risk notice (s.26(3)(a)) until the Authority's Oct 2024 draft transfer-instruments directive is final. dpa.gov.lk 'dates of operation' page is stale. Health-sector rows medium confidence.

NP.name: Nepal

laws.name: Privacy Act, 2075 (2018)
laws.citation: Act No. 14 of 2075; s.12 consent and purpose, s.26 body corporate data, s.27(2)(d) health as sensitive

laws.name: NMC Telemedicine Guidelines for Registered Medical Practitioners (May 2020)
laws.citation: Telemedicine reserved to NMC-registered practitioners; no remote prescribing of Category A drugs

laws.name: Public Health Service Act 2075 (2018) and Regulation 2077 (2020)
laws.citation: Health services by licensed institutions and registered professionals

healthcare_rules: Do not describe this as telemedicine; in Nepal it is reserved to NMC-registered practitioners. Refer anything about the person's own condition to an NMC-registered doctor.
Never advise on obtaining Category A (narcotic or poisonous) drugs, which Nepal does not allow even doctors to prescribe remotely.
NP.regulator: No data protection authority (privacy complaints go to the District Court); health: Nepal Medical Council (https://nmc.org.np)
NP.notes: Health is 'sensitive' under Privacy Act s.27(2)(d), but the s.27(1) ban targets public bodies. Unresolved: s.23(1) says only persons authorised by law may collect or process personal information (unclear for private apps), and reach over a foreign company with no Nepal presence is untested. IT and Cyber Security Bill 2082 lapsed when the House was dissolved (Sep 2025); it would add a destroy-after-purpose rule. Nepal has blocked unregistered platforms (social media, Sep 2025). s.6 protects women's reproductive-health data.

BT.name: Bhutan

laws.name: Information, Communications and Media Act of Bhutan 2018, Chapter 17
laws.citation: ss.336-351; s.464(89) health as sensitive; s.341 opt-in; s.343 recipient contracts; s.350 children

laws.name: Medical and Health Council Act of Bhutan 2002
laws.citation: Practice requires BMHC registration

laws.name: Medicines Act of the Kingdom of Bhutan 2003
laws.citation: Medicines and their promotion (BFDA)

BT.notes: ICM Act Chapter 17 treats health as sensitive; transfers allowed if recipients are contractually bound to Chapter 17 (s.343) and we stay liable (s.342). Extraterritorial reach (s.4) over a foreign app is plausible but untested. Parliament and GovTech sites were unreachable, so a standalone Personal Data Protection Act passed in 2024-2026 cannot be ruled out; confirm with Bhutanese counsel. BMHC and Medicines Act provisions not re-verified. Gelephu Mindfulness City has its own regime (not checked).

MV.name: Maldives

laws.name: Telemedicine Guideline for Healthcare Professionals
laws.citation: MoH, MOH-QA/G/23/146-1, v3 18 Apr 2024; HIPAA-or-equivalent hosting benchmark

laws.name: Health Services Act and Medical Records Regulation
laws.citation: Law No. 29/2015; Regulation 2019/R-1070

laws.name: Medicine Regulation
laws.citation: 2014/R-46 (amended 2016/R-49), r.7.13 no promotion of prescription medicines

healthcare_rules: Do not promote or recommend a specific prescription medicine or brand; Maldives Medicine Regulation 2014/R-46 r.7.13 bans promoting prescription medicines.
MV.regulator: No data protection authority; health: Ministry of Health (https://health.gov.mv) and Maldives Food and Drug Authority (https://mfda.gov.mv)
MV.notes: No data protection act in the Attorney General's database (laws through No. 16/2026; the database warns it may be incomplete); recheck mvlaw.gov.mv for a Personal Data Protection Act before launch. The MoH Telemedicine Guideline binds professionals, but its HIPAA-or-equivalent hosting standard is the benchmark for our processors. Child Rights Protection Act 19/2019 child definition not re-verified. No 'Medicines and Therapeutic Goods Act 2019' exists; the framework is Law 75/78 plus Regulation 2014/R-46.

AF.name: Afghanistan

laws.name: OFAC Afghanistan-related sanctions (General Licenses 14-20)
laws.citation: Not comprehensive (OFAC FAQ 951); Taliban and Haqqani Network are SDN-listed; GL 20 of 25 Feb 2022

healthcare_rules: Assume care may be hard to reach, especially for women: give clear warning signs and practical steps to get to the nearest hospital or clinic rather than only saying to see a doctor.
AF.regulator: No data protection authority; US side: OFAC (https://ofac.treasury.gov/sanctions-programs-and-country-information/afghanistan-related-sanctions)
AF.notes: Persist: no Afghan data law, and Afghanistan is not under comprehensive OFAC sanctions (FAQ 951; GL 20), so a consumer service is allowed if we never contract with or take payment from SDNs (Taliban, Haqqani). The research did NOT check whether Anthropic and OpenAI support Afghanistan; verify both country lists and switch to unavailable if either excludes it. De facto Taliban rule makes law uncertain, and health, reproductive and mental-health data carry high user risk (2024 Virtue and Vice law); research urges minimal retention.
